source_review.notes: Reviewed current PostgreSQL 18 text-search, GIN, and index-maintenance documentation; current SQLite FTS5, MySQL 8.4 natural/Boolean full-text, and Lucene 10.3.1 format documentation; the Stanford IR text; the Robertson-Zaragoza BM25 paper; and Zobel-Moffat bibliographic metadata. Nine direct destinations were retained locally after successful retrieval. The ACM DOI and metadata resolved, but its landing page rejected automated content retrieval with HTTP 403. Product behavior is explicitly version/current-documentation scoped.

evidence: Checked term dictionary, posting list, document and term frequency, positions, offsets, analyzer version, candidate set, live universe, and recheck definitions.
Checked Boolean intersection, union, and relative complement notation against the declared compatible snapshot/document universe.
Checked phrase-position witnesses and the stated BM25 IDF and length-normalized saturation formula.
Checked ranking tuples, stable secondary document ordering, freshness watermarks, and versioned continuation state.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Scores are consistently labeled ranking values rather than probabilities, and the BM25 formula is one declared variant rather than a universal definition.

evidence: Independently reconstructed the four-document term/position map from the declared ASCII analyzer.
Recomputed database AND systems candidates as (1,3) and visibility-filtered results as (1).
Recomputed the adjacent database-systems phrase result as document 1 and phrase OR rank as documents (2,4).
Recomputed the text-plus-search frequency ordering as ((4,3),(1,2),(2,2)) with document ID tie-breaking.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The independent implementation printed independent_invariants=True and did not import or execute the chapter implementation.

evidence: Re-derived exact AND as membership in every required posting list and OR as membership in at least one list.
Re-derived NOT as set difference relative to a declared live positive universe, not an implicit global complement.
Re-derived phrase adjacency from positional witnesses pos(next)=pos(previous)+1 rather than term co-occurrence.
Re-derived why candidate generation followed by authoritative visibility, authorization, and residual recheck preserves result semantics when postings are stale or lossy.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The arguments assume compatible analyzer/index generations, document identities, snapshot rules, and correct posting maintenance.

evidence: Reviewed empty terms/documents, repeated terms, stop-word-only input, long tokens, phrase gaps, prefix/fuzzy fan-out, and Boolean NOT without a live universe.
Reviewed composed/decomposed Unicode, Turkish I, CJK without spaces, code identifiers, punctuation, apostrophes, hyphens, emoji, synonyms, stemming collisions, and analyzer mismatch.
Reviewed inserts, updates, deletes, dead versions, duplicate/out-of-order events, pending lists, segment merges, tombstones, disk-full, crash replay, corruption, replica lag, and rebuild catch-up.
Reviewed stale statistics, tied scores, pagination drift, authorization filtering, tenant isolation, facet/snippet leakage, expansion denial of service, cancellation, and sensitive query logging.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The executable analyzer is intentionally ASCII-only; Unicode and language behavior are design/review cases, never implied capabilities of that model.

evidence: The repository verifier matched exact seven-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status after the ASCII implementation correction.
The model checks every posting occurrence against independently analyzed token counts and exact stored positions.
The model checks Boolean candidates, visibility filtering, phrase adjacency, OR semantics, ranking order, and invisible-document exclusion.
Draft validation accepted exact front matter, section order, ten examples, five exercises/answers, local links, and executable evidence before stopping only for the digest-bound review.
invariant_checking.notes: The finite model omits production tokenization, compressed persistence, SQL/MVCC internals, WAL, concurrency, authorization, distributed delivery, BM25, and performance.

evidence: Reviewed the Boolean soundness argument line by line under exact-posting and compatible-snapshot assumptions.
Reviewed the phrase argument to ensure order/adjacency requires positions or authoritative recheck.
Reviewed the candidate/recheck argument for stale, dead, lossy, and unauthorized postings.
Reviewed all exercise answers for analyzer migration, merge publication/recovery, BM25 recomputation, continuation stability, evaluation, and rollback obligations.
proof_review.notes: No proof of tokenizer linguistic quality, compression optimality, database recovery implementation, optimizer choice, relevance dominance, or production safety is claimed.

evidence: Boolean and phrase statements identify the exact-posting, compatible-universe, and positional assumptions required for soundness.
The executable artifact is explicitly a tiny ASCII finite model with named omissions.
Toy frequency rank is never presented as BM25, calibrated relevance, or probability.
Audited exact, compatible, current, authoritative, complete, sound, correct, stable, and production language for scope and assumptions.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Empirical guidance is conditioned on workload evidence, language/analyzer versions, security constraints, and measured operational state.

evidence: The standard-library inverted-index model executed successfully through the repository verifier.
A separate implementation independently reproduced Boolean, phrase, visibility, OR, and ranking results.
Nine cited destinations were successfully retrieved and retained; the ACM DOI metadata resolved while automated landing-page retrieval returned HTTP 403.
Performance and relevance claims require corpus slices, recall/precision/NDCG/MRR, freshness, candidates, expansions, rechecks, merge debt, I/O, and latency evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live DBMS/FTS extension, persistent segment, GIN page, MVCC snapshot, WAL recovery, concurrent merge, multilingual corpus, relevance study, or benchmark was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter separates analyzer semantics, dictionary/posting representation, Boolean and positional candidate generation, ranking, authoritative recheck, and derived-index lifecycle.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed analyzer/ranker versioning, native versus external consistency, pending/segment debt, MVCC and delete handling, crash-safe publication, backfill/cutover/rollback, limits, authorization, observability, and production evaluation.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet, transparent executable trace, ten distinct worked examples, and five exercises progress from analyzer and posting mechanics through ranking, failure recovery, migration, security, and evaluation.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. The chapter does not certify a production analyzer, posting codec, database extension, MVCC/WAL path, distributed search service, relevance model, benchmark, authorization policy, or workload fitness.
